nodes.title: Expose window reference handles (from xdg_foreign, XID, etc)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Windowing systems allow to reference windows of other apps using some kind of platform specific tokens. For example wayland has the `xdg_foreign` protocol, X11 uses XIDs. I am not familiar with Windows or MacOS APIs, but i am sure they have something similar. Currently Electron has no way to get these for own windows, so they cannot be exported to other applications.

An example (and the motivation for this issue) are XDG Desktop portals. They describe the reasoning here: https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/window-identifiers.html. As of now, using portals from within an Electron application requires passing an empty string as the window identifier, so dialogs do not get placed correctly.

Internally, they are already detected and used by chromium and electron (via [`ExportWindowHandle`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/4ae8411d3e994ca1445c358a858f16fc9bdf40e2/ui/linux/linux_ui_delegate.h#L44)), so it shoud merely be a case of exposing them on a public API.

### Proposed Solution

Add a method to `BaseWindow` that returns the platform dependent window identifier handle.

### Alternatives Considered

Use `getNativeWindowHandle`, and write platform specific code that somehow talks witht the compositor itself.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: [Bug]: fs.constants.O_DIRECTORY has the wrong value on linux-arm64, so open() on a directory fails with EINVAL
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 44.0.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version Debian forky/sid, `Linux 7.2.2 aarch64`, X11 (no window needed to reproduce) ### What arch are you using? arm64 (including Apple Silicon) ### Last Known Working Electron version 43.4.1 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior On arm64 Linux, `fs.constants` should hold the aarch64 values, and opening a directory with `O_DIRECTORY` should work: - `O_DIRECTORY` = 16384 - `O_NOFOLLOW` = 32768 - `O_DIRECT` = 65536 ### Actual Behavior They hold the x86-64 values instead, and opening a directory throws `EINVAL`: ``` $ unzip -q electron-v44.0.0-linux-arm64.zip -d x $ cd x && ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 ./electron ../repro.js arch : arm64 electron : 44.0.0 node : 24.18.1 O_DIRECTORY : 65536 (aarch64 expects 16384) O_NOFOLLOW : 131072 (aarch64 expects 32768) O_DIRECT : 16384 (aarch64 expects 65536) open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : EINVAL <-- the bug $ node ../repro.js # system Node, same machine, same kernel arch : arm64 electron : undefined node : 24.20.0 O_DIRECTORY : 16384 (aarch64 expects 16384) O_NOFOLLOW : 32768 (aarch64 expects 32768) O_DIRECT : 65536 (aarch64 expects 65536) open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK ``` Two user-visible consequences: 1. Any app that opens a directory (a common durable-write / fsync-the-directory step) fails with `EINVAL` on arm64. That is how I found this: a shipping Electron app persists none of its state on Linux arm64, because every one of its directory writes throws. 2. `O_NOFOLLOW` silently becomes `O_LARGEFILE`, a no-op on 64-bit. Code passing `O_NOFOLLOW` to guard against a planted symlink still succeeds and gets no error, so the protection is gone with no symptom at all. ### Testcase Gist URL No Fiddle gist: the repro needs no window and no Electron API, and it only reproduces on arm64 hardware. The eight-line `repro.js` above is standalone — run it with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` against any affected `linux-arm64` release asset. ```js const fs = require('fs'); const c = fs.constants; console.log('arch :', process.arch); console.log('electron :', process.versions.electron); console.log('node :', process.versions.node); console.log('O_DIRECTORY :', c.O_DIRECTORY, '(aarch64 expects 16384)'); console.log('O_NOFOLLOW :', c.O_NOFOLLOW, '(aarch64 expects 32768)'); console.log('O_DIRECT :', c.O_DIRECT, '(aarch64 expects 65536)'); try { fs.closeSync(fs.openSync('/tmp', c.O_RDONLY | c.O_DIRECTORY | c.O_NOFOLLOW)); console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK'); } catch (e) { console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) :', e.code, '<-- the bug'); } ``` ### Additional Information Affected releases. I ran the repro against each official `electron-v-linux-arm64.zip`, on the same machine: | published | version | `O_DIRECTORY` | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2026-08-11 | 42.9.0 | 16384 | ok | | 2026-08-15 | 42.9.1 | 16384 | ok | | 2026-08-16 | 42.9.2 | 16384 | ok | | 2026-08-18 | 42.9.3 | 16384 | ok | | 2026-08-19 | 43.4.1 | 16384 | ok — last good | | 2026-08-24 | 42.10.0 | 65536 | **broken** | | 2026-08-25 | 42.10.1 | 65536 | **broken** | | 2026-08-25 | 44.0.0 | 65536 | **broken** | Also verified good, further back: 43.4.0 and 42.8.1 (2026-08-11), 43.3.0 (2026-08-04), 43.2.0 (2026-07-21), 43.0.0 (2026-06-30). Not tested: `linux-armv7l`, which also overrides the generic fcntl values and may be affected the same way. `linux-x64` cannot show the bug, since there the generic values are the correct ones.
In-depth investigation

arm64 is one of the architectures that override the `asm-generic` fcntl defaults, in `arch/arm64/include/uapi/asm/fcntl.h`, and it swaps exactly two pairs: | constant | aarch64 | generic / x86-64 | | --- | --- | --- | | `O_DIRECTORY` | 16384 (`040000`) | 65536 (`0200000`) | | `O_NOFOLLOW` | 32768 (`0100000`) | 131072 (`0400000`) | | `O_DIRECT` | 65536 (`0200000`) | 16384 (`040000`) | So on the affected builds, a request for `O_DIRECTORY` reaches the kernel as `O_DIRECT`, and `O_DIRECT` on a directory returns `EINVAL` — which accounts for the observed error exactly. Conversely `O_NOFOLLOW` arrives as `O_LARGEFILE`. `node_constants.cc` picks these values up from the UAPI headers at compile time, so this looks like the linux-arm64 build environment resolving `asm/fcntl.h` to the generic definitions rather than the arm64 ones — a sysroot or header search path problem, not anything in the Electron or Node source tree. Two observations support that reading: - The break spans three release branches (`42-x-y` and `main`), and correlates with publication date rather than with branch or commit: everything published up to 2026-08-19 is fine, everything from 2026-08-24 on is broken. - 42.9.3 (good) and 42.10.0 (broken) ship the identical Node, 24.18.1. So no Node change is involved. My guess is a toolchain or sysroot image update landing in that window, but I have no visibility into the release infrastructure.

--- *Disclosure, per the [AI Tool Policy](https://github.com/electron/governance/blob/main/policy/ai.md): I investigated this with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5), which also drafted this report. Everything above was produced and verified on my own aarch64 machine, and I have reviewed it and can answer questions about it.*

## Preflight checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

## Electron version

44.0.0 (also 42.10.0, 42.10.1)

## What operating system(s) are you using?

Debian (forky/sid), aarch64

## Operating System Version

Linux aarch64, ext4

## What arch are you using?

arm64

## Last Known Working Electron version

43.4.1 (published 2026-08-19)

## Expected Behavior

On aarch64 Linux, `fs.constants` should carry the arm64 values defined in
`arch/arm64/include/uapi/asm/fcntl.h`:

| constant | aarch64 | generic / x86-64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `O_DIRECTORY` | 16384 (`040000`) | 65536 (`0200000`) |
| `O_NOFOLLOW` | 32768 (`0100000`) | 131072 (`0400000`) |
| `O_DIRECT` | 65536 (`0200000`) | 16384 (`040000`) |

arm64 is one of the architectures that override the `asm-generic` defaults, and it
swaps exactly these two pairs.

## Actual Behavior

Affected linux-arm64 builds report the **generic/x86-64** values. On arm64 those bit
patterns mean `O_DIRECT | O_LARGEFILE`, so any `open()` that asks for
`O_DIRECTORY` actually asks for `O_DIRECT`, and opening a directory with `O_DIRECT`
returns `EINVAL`.

```
$ unzip -q electron-v44.0.0-linux-arm64.zip -d x
$ cd x && ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 ./electron ../repro.js
arch            : arm64
electron        : 44.0.0
node            : 24.18.1
O_DIRECTORY     : 65536 (aarch64 expects 16384)
O_NOFOLLOW      : 131072 (aarch64 expects 32768)
O_DIRECT        : 16384 (aarch64 expects 65536)
open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : EINVAL   <-- the bug

$ node ../repro.js          # system Node, same machine, same kernel
arch            : arm64
electron        : undefined
node            : 24.20.0
O_DIRECTORY     : 16384 (aarch64 expects 16384)
O_NOFOLLOW      : 32768 (aarch64 expects 32768)
O_DIRECT        : 65536 (aarch64 expects 65536)
open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK
```

## Testcase Gist URL / repro.js

```js
const fs = require('fs');
const c = fs.constants;
console.log('arch            :', process.arch);
console.log('electron        :', process.versions.electron);
console.log('node            :', process.versions.node);
console.log('O_DIRECTORY     :', c.O_DIRECTORY, '(aarch64 expects 16384)');
console.log('O_NOFOLLOW      :', c.O_NOFOLLOW, '(aarch64 expects 32768)');
console.log('O_DIRECT        :', c.O_DIRECT, '(aarch64 expects 65536)');
try {
  fs.closeSync(fs.openSync('/tmp', c.O_RDONLY | c.O_DIRECTORY | c.O_NOFOLLOW));
  console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) : OK');
} catch (e) {
  console.log('open("/tmp", O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) :', e.code, '<-- the bug');
}
```

## Additional Information

### This tracks the build date, not the branch or the Node version

I probed the official `electron-v<version>-linux-arm64.zip` release assets, one by one,
on the same aarch64 machine:

| published | version | `O_DIRECTORY` | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-06-30 | 43.0.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-07-21 | 43.2.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-04 | 42.8.1 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-04 | 43.3.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-11 | 42.9.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-11 | 43.4.0 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-15 | 42.9.1 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-16 | 42.9.2 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-18 | 42.9.3 | 16384 | correct |
| 2026-08-19 | 43.4.1 | 16384 | correct — **last good** |
| 2026-08-24 | 42.10.0 | 65536 | **broken — first bad** |
| 2026-08-25 | 42.10.1 | 65536 | **broken** |
| 2026-08-25 | 44.0.0 | 65536 | **broken** |

Two points worth stressing:

1. The break spans **three different release branches** (`42-x-y` and `main`). The only
   thing the bad builds share is that they were produced after 2026-08-19.
2. **42.9.3 (good) and 42.10.0 (bad) ship the identical Node, 24.18.1.** So this is not
   a Node change — `node_constants.cc` picks these values up from the UAPI headers at
   compile time, which points at the linux-arm64 build environment (sysroot / header
   search path resolving `asm/fcntl.h` to the generic definitions instead of the arm64
   ones) rather than at anything in the Electron or Node source tree.

My guess is a sysroot or toolchain image update landing in that window, but I have no
visibility into the release infrastructure.

### Impact

This is quiet and nasty rather than loud:

- `open()` on a directory with `O_DIRECTORY` fails with `EINVAL` — the failure mode that
  led me here. Any app doing a durable-write / `fsync`-the-directory dance on arm64 is
  broken.
- **`O_NOFOLLOW` silently becomes `O_LARGEFILE`, which is a no-op on 64-bit.** Code that
  passes `O_NOFOLLOW` to defend against symlink swaps still opens successfully and gets
  no error — the protection is simply gone. That one has security consequences and
  produces no symptom at all.
- Conversely, `O_DIRECT` now means `O_DIRECTORY`.

I found this because a shipping Electron app (Claude Desktop 1.40609.0 arm64, on Electron
42.10.0) fails to write any of its state on Linux arm64: every private-directory write
throws `EINVAL`, so nothing is ever persisted. Filed separately with that vendor.

Not tested: `linux-armv7l`, which also overrides the generic fcntl values and may well be
affected the same way. `linux-x64` cannot show the bug, since there the generic values are
the correct ones.

x64

43.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

StatusNotifierItem appears normally

### Actual Behavior

No StatusNotifierItem appeared, with log output:

```
[3:0829/183302.771226:ERROR:dbus/bus.cc:570] Failed to get the ownership of org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-3-1: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown
[3:0829/183302.772046:ERROR:dbus/bus.cc:587] org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-3-1 is not owned by the bus
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/YUCLing/bf1ee0764b90ac2a2f0181f67b4460c1

### Additional Information

This is another issue introduced by Chromium's changes since [crrev.com/c/8043132](https://crrev.com/c/8043132), and this is different with #52674. The issue only appears when running in environment like Flatpak that [restricts acquiring ownership of the name `StatusNotifierItem-PID-ID`](https://docs.flatpak.org/en/latest/desktop-integration.html#statusnotifier), it's still present while #52674 is fixed.

To reproduce with the gist using Flatpak, install the latest Flatpak runtime, run:
```sh
flatpak run \
  --share=network \ # The gist downloads the icon from network
  --share=ipc \
  --socket=wayland \
  --talk-name=org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher \ # Chromium needs to first be able talk with StatusNotifierWatcher to begin with the creation.
  --filesystem=/path/to/gist/app/folder \
  --command=sh \
  org.freedesktop.Platform
/path/to/gist/app/folder/app --no-sandbox # Sandbox doesn't work in Flatpak environment
```

Downloading PDFs with changes should work.

When trying to download a modified PDF "with your changes" the following error is thrown:

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/stefanodaker/d6dabb7f5cf175938f97a8fb231b77f1

### Additional Information

This bug was already present in earlier electron versions and was fixed, see [issue](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51041) and [pr](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51042). The bug is reproducible with the gist of the original issue.

nodes.title: Linux + useSharedTexture = black texture
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

44.0.0 (also reproduced on 42.3.3)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

CachyOS (Arch), kernel 7.1.3-1-cachyos, x86_64. KDE Plasma 6 / kwin_wayland, and separately a bare Xorg session on a spare VT.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

none on Linux (useSharedTexture working great on MacOS and Windows)

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

With `webPreferences.offscreen.useSharedTexture: true`, the dma-buf referenced by
`textureInfo.handle.nativePixmap` should contain the rendered page.

### Actual Behavior

The `paint` event fires, `textureInfo` is fully populated and plausible, and the dma-buf is a real,
importable allocation of exactly the expected size — but every byte of it is zero.

This is **not** #49247. There, `paint` never fires with a texture. Here the handle arrives and is
structurally correct; only its contents are missing. It also reproduces where
`supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport` is `true`, which is the configuration #49247 treats as working.

The clearest way to see it uses only Electron's own APIs — `sharedTexture.importSharedTexture`,
`sendSharedTexture`, and `VideoFrame.copyTo`. No native addon, no external consumer:

Under KDE Plasma / Wayland:

```
paint#5  supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport=false  modifier=0  stride=5120
imported textureId=578d48a9-...
VideoFrame 1280x720 format=BGRA bytes=3686400
nonzeroPixels=0/921600  firstPixel=[0,0,0,0]
```

And on a bare Xorg session on a spare VT, where the flag is `true` — the configuration #49247
treats as working — the same script, unchanged:

```
session: tty  DISPLAY=:1  WAYLAND_DISPLAY=unset
paint#5  supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport=true  modifier=0  stride=5120
imported textureId=14f9f92c-186a-4e2d-ac3a-07d73971ff53
VideoFrame 1280x720 format=BGRA bytes=3686400
nonzeroPixels=0/921600  firstPixel=[0,0,0,0]
```

The page under test is a solid, continuously animating background, so a correct buffer cannot be
zero. The A/B against Chromium's other output path, same URL, same switches, same machine, differing
only in `useSharedTexture`:

| offscreen mode | non-zero pixels |
| --- | --- |
| `useSharedTexture: false` (CPU bitmap) | 921600 / 921600 |
| `useSharedTexture: true` (dma-buf) | 0 / 921600 |

Chromium renders the page; only the shared-texture export is empty.

#### What has been ruled out

Four independent readers agree the memory is zero — Electron's own import + WebCodecs readback; a
`VK_EXT_image_drm_format_modifier` import plus GPU copy; a CPU `mmap` with `DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC`; and
a third-party Vulkan consumer. The CPU mapping shares none of the Vulkan importers' assumptions
about modifier, stride, memory type or layout, and still reads zero. Zeros rather than garbage
argues the memory is genuinely zero rather than correct bytes read through a wrong layout.

Also ruled out:

- **Timing.** Reading 3 seconds after the paint, while still holding the lease, is unchanged.
- **Warm-up.** The 25th paint of a continuously animating page is unchanged.
- **First-frame effects.** Same at paint 1, 5, 10 and 25.
- **Content.** Same for a `data:` URL, a local app, and a fully loaded `https://youtube.com`.
- **Format.** Same for `argb` (stride 5120) and `rgbaf16` (stride 10240).
- **Electron version.** Same on 42.3.3 and 44.0.0.
- **Session type.** Same under Wayland and under a real Xorg session (not XWayland).
- **Vulkan/ANGLE coherence.** See below.

#### Interaction with #49247, and one caution

On Wayland, Chromium logs `Unable to initialize SkSurface` and delivers `paint` with no texture,
exactly as #49247 reports. Adding **`--use-angle=vulkan`** alongside `--enable-features=Vulkan`
clears that: ANGLE moves onto Vulkan (`ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.341, RTX 4090)`), the error stops,
and a real dma-buf is delivered. `--enable-features=Vulkan` on its own is not enough, and
`--ignore-gpu-blocklist` on its own is worse than neither, because it enables Vulkan while leaving
ANGLE on GL — which is also when Ozone reports Wayland and Vulkan to be incompatible.

That may be useful to #49247 on its own. But it does not fix the buffer, and neither does Xorg. On a
bare Xorg session `supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport` flips to `true` and all four readers still see
zero.

The caution: the "Ubuntu 24.04 Xorg — works fine" result in #49247 is evidenced by a `console.log`
of `textureInfo`, which is metadata. That is the same metadata this machine prints under Xorg,
`supportsZeroCopyWebGpuImport: true` included. I could not find anywhere in that thread, or in the
shared-texture docs, where the *pixels* are read back and checked. So the two observations may not
conflict: the handle can be correct while the buffer behind it is never filled, and only a consumer
that samples it would notice. If someone with a known-good Linux setup can run the script below and
report a non-zero count, that would localise this to NVIDIA immediately.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/marcdownie/2938b49759c9516ff4612ade344d6f22

### Additional Information

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, proprietary driver 610.43.02. The machine also has an AMD Raphael
iGPU, but Chromium runs on the NVIDIA card throughout (confirmed via
`WEBGL_debug_renderer_info`); the AMD path could not be tested, because restricting the Vulkan ICD
to RADV prevents the GPU process from starting against this NVIDIA-driven display.

`--ozone-platform=x11` inside a Wayland session is XWayland and is not a substitute: the GPU process
dies with exit code 139, matching #49247. The Xorg results above are from a genuine X server started
on a spare VT.

nodes.title: Tracking: documented APIs without spec test coverage (docs/api vs spec audit)
nodes.body:
An audit of the documented API surface in `docs/api/*.md` (main @ ffd19de9) against the test suite under `spec/`. Method: static cross-reference — every documented method/property/event/constructor/`<webview>` attribute heading was searched for references anywhere in `spec/` (dedicated `api-*-spec.ts`, any other spec, or `spec/ts-smoke` type tests).

Scope: 1,577 documented API items across 76 `docs/api` files. `docs/api/structures/` (110 files) plus `command-line-switches`, `environment-variables`, `corner-smoothing-css`, and `window-open` were excluded as non-testable surfaces.

## Overall numbers

| | items | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| Referenced somewhere in `spec/` | 1,300 | 82% |
| Referenced **only** in `spec/ts-smoke` type tests | 40 | 3% |
| **No reference anywhere in `spec/`** | **237** | **15%** |

## Headline gaps

- **`pushNotifications`: 0/3 covered, no spec file at all** — the entire macOS APNS surface (`registerForAPNSNotifications`, `unregisterForAPNSNotifications`, `received-apns-notification`) is untested.
- **`BaseWindow` has no dedicated spec file** despite 187 documented items. Its coverage is almost entirely incidental via `BrowserWindow` tests; 30 items have no reference at all.
- **`unresponsive`/`responsive` events** (on both `BrowserWindow` and `WebContents`) have zero references anywhere in `spec/` — not even a string match — despite being the primary hang-detection API.
- **`Tray` interaction surface is essentially untested**: every interaction event (`click` variants, `mouse-*`, all `drag-*`/`drop-*`), `balloon-click`/`balloon-closed`, `getGUID`, `removeBalloon`.
- **All four `screen` DIP conversion methods** (`screenToDipPoint`, `dipToScreenPoint`, `screenToDipRect`, `dipToScreenRect`) are untested.

## Per-module task list (worst offenders)

Counts are uncovered/total documented items, where "uncovered" = no reference in `spec/` or ts-smoke-only. Item lists below name the most notable gaps, not all of them — full item-level detail is in the linked report.

- [ ] **pushNotifications — 3/3**: whole module (`registerForAPNSNotifications`, `unregisterForAPNSNotifications`, `received-apns-notification`); no spec file exists
- [ ] **webContents — 37/200**: `unresponsive`/`responsive`, device emulation (`enableDeviceEmulation`/`disableDeviceEmulation`), caret browsing (`setCaretBrowsingEnabled`/`isCaretBrowsingEnabled`), selection/scroll helpers (`centerSelection`, `unselect`, `scrollToTop`, `scrollToBottom`, `adjustSelection`), `copyImageAt`, `saveVideoFrameAs`, `isBeingCaptured`, `isWaitingForResponse`, `inspectSharedWorker`/`inspectServiceWorker`, `replaceMisspelling`, `input-event`, `cursor-changed`, `update-target-url`, `preferred-size-changed`
- [ ] **BrowserWindow — 35/204**: `unresponsive`/`responsive`, `will-resize`/`will-move`/`moved`, `query-session-end`/`session-end`, `app-command`, `flashFrame`, `hookWindowMessage` family, thumbar/thumbnail methods (`setThumbarButtons`, `setThumbnailClip`, `setThumbnailToolTip`), `setOverlayIcon`, `setBackgroundMaterial`, `isSnapped`/`snapped`, `focusOnWebView`/`blurWebView`
- [ ] **BaseWindow — 31/187**: no dedicated spec file; largely the same window-management gaps as BrowserWindow (`will-resize`/`will-move`/`moved`, `session-end` events, `hookWindowMessage` family, thumbar methods, `flashFrame`, `getContentView`, `isModal`, `isNormal`, `setBackgroundMaterial`)
- [ ] **session — 25/93**: `clearCodeCaches`, `clearHostResolverCache`, `setUSBProtectedClassesHandler`, `setBluetoothPairingHandler`, the spellchecker surface (`setSpellCheckerEnabled`, `isSpellCheckerEnabled`, `getSpellCheckerLanguages`, `availableSpellCheckerLanguages`, all four `spellcheck-dictionary-*` events), device add/remove events (`hid-*`, `serial-port-*`, `usb-device-*`), `getCacheSize`, `flushStorageData`, `closeAllConnections`
- [ ] **app — 24/114**: `will-quit`, `will-finish-launching`, `gpu-info-update`, macOS activity/Handoff surface (`continue-activity` family, `updateCurrentActivity`, `invalidateCurrentActivity`, `resignCurrentActivity`), `open-file`/`open-url`, `hasSingleInstanceLock`, `setAppUserModelId`, `moveToApplicationsFolder`, `toastActivatorCLSID`
- [ ] **Tray — 20/36**: every interaction event — `click` (behavioral), `right-click`, `double-click`, `middle-click`, `mouse-up`/`mouse-down`/`mouse-enter`/`mouse-leave`/`mouse-move`, `drag-enter`/`drag-leave`/`drag-end`, `drop`/`drop-files`/`drop-text` — plus `balloon-click`/`balloon-closed`, `removeBalloon`, `getGUID`
- [ ] **`<webview>` tag — 24/113**: mostly repeats of the webContents method gaps (`centerSelection`, `unselect`, scroll helpers, `adjustSelection`, `replaceMisspelling`, `inspect*Worker`, `isWaitingForResponse`) plus attributes `plugins`, `nodeintegrationinsubframes`, `enableblinkfeatures`/`disableblinkfeatures` and events `load-commit`, `update-target-url`
- [ ] **systemPreferences — 10/26**: macOS notification subscription surface (`postNotification`, `postLocalNotification`, all `unsubscribe*Notification`), `askForMediaAccess`, `accent-color-changed`, `isSwipeTrackingFromScrollEventsEnabled`
- [ ] **powerMonitor — 8/16**: `lock-screen`/`unlock-screen`, `thermal-state-change`, `speed-limit-change`, `user-did-become-active`/`user-did-resign-active` (`on-ac`/`on-battery` are ts-smoke-only)
- [ ] **screen — 7/12**: all four DIP conversion methods (`screenToDipPoint`, `dipToScreenPoint`, `screenToDipRect`, `dipToScreenRect`); `display-added`/`display-removed`/`display-metrics-changed` are ts-smoke-only
- [ ] **Notification — 5/30**: `reply` and `action` events, `handleActivation`, `urgency`, `timeoutType`
- [ ] **TouchBar item classes — 12 items** across `TouchBarScrubber` (4), `TouchBarColorPicker`, `TouchBarLabel`, `TouchBarSegmentedControl`, `TouchBarSlider`, `TouchBarButton` (2 each) — mostly instance properties never read/written in tests

## Platform split of the 237 unreferenced items

- 55 macOS-only
- 40 Windows-only
- 145 with no platform restriction — testable on the existing Linux CI path today

## Full report

Item-by-item breakdown (all 1,577 items, per-module tables, tier for each item): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/671ee4f0-4aef-4f61-b2b9-80cb5bc34f2a

## Caveats

- This is **static string matching**: an item counts as "covered" if its name is referenced anywhere in `spec/`. A reference is not a behavioral assertion — common short names (`show`, `focus`, `id`) inflate apparent coverage, so the real behavioral gap is larger than 15%.
- Conversely, some items may be exercised indirectly (e.g. via helpers) without a name match, though heading-level matching makes this rare.
- Many gaps are platform-bound (Tray interactions, thumbar, APNS) and genuinely hard to drive in CI — the task list is for triage, not an assertion that every item is automatable.

nodes.title: [Bug]: Linux safeStorage kwallet backend uses KWallet4-era D-Bus path on Plasma 6 and --password-store is ignored
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.8.1 (Chromium 148.0.7778.280) — as shipped in VS Code 1.133/1.134/1.135; all three reproduce.

### What operating system are you using?

Arch Linux x86_64, KDE Plasma 6.7.4 (Wayland), kwallet 6.29 (`kwalletd6`; no kwalletd5 present)

### What architecture are you using?

x64

### Last Working Electron Version

Unknown — this reproduces on every Electron-42-era build I tested. The documented `--password-store` workaroutes (e.g. `kwallet5`) reportedly worked on earlier Electron generations.

### Expected Behavior

On KDE Plasma 6, `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()` should return `true`: kwalletd6 is running, enabled, the default wallet is open, and it serves the KWallet D-Bus API at `/modules/kwalletd5` and `/modules/kwalletd6` (and owns all three bus names `org.kde.kwalletd`, `org.kde.kwalletd5`, `org.kde.kwalletd6`).

`--password-store` should select the backend (per the Chromium `key_storage_util_linux.cc` contract and VS Code's documentation of this flag for Electron apps).

### Actual Behavior

Two distinct problems:

**1. The kwallet backend unconditionally uses the KWallet4-era service path.** OSCrypt probes `org.kde.KWallet.isEnabled` at **`/modules/kwalletd`**, which kwalletd6 does not export → `UnknownObject` → OSCrypt initializes no backend → `safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable()` returns `false` and secrets fall back to the hardcoded-password "v11" encryption.

**2. `--password-store` has no effect on OSCrypt selection.** Tested as a fresh main process:

| `--password-store` | `Selected backend for OSCrypt` | object path probed |
|---|---|---|
| *(unset / detect)* | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |
| `kwallet5` | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |
| `kwallet6` | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |
| `gnome-libsecret` | `KWALLET` | `/modules/kwalletd` |

Setting `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KDE` and `KDE_SESSION_VERSION=6` explicitly does not change the outcome. Notably, the `Password storage detected desktop environment: ...` VLOG from `key_storage_util_linux.cc` (documented in VS Code's keychain troubleshooting) never appears at all — the whole detection/selection stage seems bypassed.

### Testcase Gist / Code To Reproduce

Any Electron 42 app on Plasma 6:

```js
// main.js
const { app, safeStorage } = require('electron');
app.whenReady().then(() => {
  console.log('isEncryptionAvailable:', safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable());
  console.log('getSelectedStorageBackend:', safeStorage.getSelectedStorageBackend());
  app.exit(0);
});
```

```sh
npx electron . --password-store=kwallet5 --enable-logging=stderr --vmodule="*/components/os_crypt/*=2"
```

stderr:

```
VERBOSE1:components/os_crypt/sync/key_storage_linux.cc:116] Selected backend for OSCrypt: KWALLET
WARNING:dbus/object_proxy.cc:570] Failed to call method: org.kde.KWallet.isEnabled: object_path= /modules/kwalletd: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownObject: No such object path '/modules/kwalletd'
ERROR:components/os_crypt/sync/kwallet_dbus.cc:113] Error contacting kwalletd (isEnabled)
ERROR:components/os_crypt/sync/kwallet_dbus.cc:82] Error contacting klauncher to start kwalletd
WARNING:components/os_crypt/sync/key_storage_linux.cc:189] OSCrypt tried KWallet but couldn't initialise.
VERBOSE1:components/os_crypt/sync/key_storage_linux.cc:135] OSCrypt did not initialize a backend.
```

Output: `isEncryptionAvailable: false`, `getSelectedStorageBackend: kwallet` — identical for every `--password-store` value.

### Additional Information

- Per the Chromium 148 source, `KWalletDBus::KWalletDBus(base::nix::DesktopEnvironment)` only picks the `kwalletd5`/`kwalletd6` constants for `DESKTOP_ENVIRONMENT_KDE5`/`KDE6`; everything else — including whatever value is being computed here — falls into the legacy `else` branch with the KWallet4 constants (`org.kde.kwalletd` + `/modules/kwalletd`).
- Consequence on disk: all app secrets stored with the `v11` prefix (hardcoded-password fallback) instead of `v10` (keyring).
- There is no way to work around this from the OS side: kwalletd6 owns `org.kde.kwalletd` and **exits with status 1** (`Failed to register name 'org.kde.kwalletd' with DBUS`) if it can't, so a proxy on the legacy bus name cannot coexist with it. Meanwhile kwalletd6 answers fine on `/modules/kwalletd5` and `/modules/kwalletd6`, so simply honoring the flag (or fixing the DE detection) would resolve it.
- Downstream impact tracked in microsoft/vscode#332559 (VS Code shows "You're running in a KDE environment but the OS keyring is not available for encryption…" on every secret write), with my full diagnosis at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332559#issuecomment-5441155367. VS Code's documented KDE 6 workaround (`--password-store=kwallet5`) no longer does anything because of problem 2.

### Electron Version

45.0.0-nightly.20260826 (current `main`, local build)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

None known

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

A zoom level set before the first navigation commits is applied once the page loads, in the zoom
modes that are meant to persist (`isolated` and `manual`) – the same way
`webPreferences: { zoomMode: 'isolated', zoomFactor: 1.5 }` already behaves.

### Actual Behavior

The call is silently dropped – no error, no return value, and `getZoomFactor()` stays at `1`:

```js
const w = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { zoomMode: 'isolated' } })
w.webContents.setZoomFactor(1.5)        // silently dropped
await w.loadURL('https://example.com')
w.webContents.getZoomFactor()           // 1 (expected 1.5)
```

`WebContentsZoomController::SetZoomLevel()` bails out on `!IsRenderFrameLive()` (no frame is live
before the first navigation commits), and the JS binding discards its `bool` result, so nothing
surfaces to the app. Expressing the same intent through web preferences does work, so the two
spellings of one intent disagree.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

The snippet above is the complete reproduction. The affected API surface is Electron-specific
(`webContents.setZoomLevel()` / `setZoomFactor()` and the `zoomMode` web preference), so there is
no Chromium equivalent to compare against. Workaround: pass the initial factor via

Other Linux ### Operating System Version Omarchy 4.0.0 (Arch-based), Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3, Wayland (Hyprland) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Unknown ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior `electron --version` prints the version string and exits 0, including when the process is started from a Linux command sandbox that returns `EPERM` for `shutdown(2)`. ### Actual Behavior Official Electron 43.4.0 (`electron-v43.4.0-linux-x64.zip`) and Slack Desktop 4.51.191 (Electron 43.4.0 / Chrome 150.0.7871.224) both abort on `--version` with SIGTRAP: ``` [2:0827/123407.303066:FATAL:content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc:41] Check failed: . shutdown: Operation not permitted (1) Trace/breakpoint trap (core dumped) ``` Exit status is 133 (128+SIGTRAP). Google Chrome 151.0.7922.173 in the **same** sandbox does not abort: `google-chrome-stable --version` prints the version, and `--headless=new --dump-dom about:blank` exits 0. Outside the sandbox, `electron --version` prints `v43.4.0` and exits 0. ### Testcase Gist URL No app code is required. Reproduction with the official binary: ```bash curl -fsSL -o electron.zip \ https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/v43.4.0/electron-v43.4.0-linux-x64.zip unzip -q electron.zip ./electron --version # v43.4.0 # Codex (or any Linux sandbox that makes shutdown(2) return EPERM): codex sandbox -- ./electron --version # FATAL:content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc:41 Check failed: . shutdown: Operation not permitted (1) ``` A direct check that the sandbox returns EPERM for `shutdown`: ```bash codex sandbox -- python3 -c 'import socket,ctypes,ctypes.util a,b=socket.socketpair(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_SEQPACKET) libc=ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("c"), use_errno=True) r=libc.shutdown(a.fileno(), 0); print("ret", r, "errno", ctypes.get_errno())' # ret -1 errno 1 ``` ### Additional Information This showed up first as a Slack Desktop 4.51.191 coredump after `slack --version` was run from a Codex bubblewrap jail (`tmux-spawn` scope, root mounted `ro,nosuid,nodev`, `/tmp/.codex` present). Slack has no public desktop issue tracker, so this is filed against Electron. Vanilla Electron 43.4.0 reproduces it. `chrome-sandbox` on the Slack package is correctly `rwsr-xr-x` root. This is not the SUID-helper-misconfigured abort.
In-depth investigation

Chromium `content/browser/sandbox_host_linux.cc` `SandboxHostLinux::Init()` does: ```cpp CHECK(socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET, 0, fds) == 0); PCHECK(0 == shutdown(child_socket_, SHUT_RD)) << "shutdown"; ``` The outer sandbox's seccomp filter returns `EPERM` for `shutdown(2)` (`man shutdown` does not list EPERM as a normal error). 44.0.0 (also 44.0.0-beta.6, 43.4.1, 43.4.2)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME with the default ubuntu-appindicators extension, Wayland and Xorg sessions

### What arch are you using?

x64, arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

44.0.0-beta.5 / 43.4.0 (icon registers; see #52674 for the separate menu problem those had), 42.x fully working

### Expected Behavior

`new Tray(image)` registers a StatusNotifierItem with `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` and the icon shows in the GNOME top bar.

### Actual Behavior

Nothing is registered with the watcher (`busctl --user get-property org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher /StatusNotifierWatcher org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher RegisteredStatusNotifierItems` never lists the app). On Wayland there is no tray icon at all; on Xorg the legacy XEmbed fallback icon appears instead.

The item calls `RegisterStatusNotifierItem("org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1")`, i.e. the well-known name with the object path appended. GNOME's watcher treats an argument that does not start with `/` as a bus name, `GetNameOwner` fails on that string, and the registration is refused, after which the SNI implementation is torn down. This came in with the cherry-pick of https://crrev.com/c/8250459 in #52951 (44-x-y) and #52952 (43-x-y); upstream fixed it a week later in https://crrev.com/c/8272040 (in Chromium 154.0.8016.0, so `main` already has it), which registers the plain well-known name and exports the item at `/StatusNotifierItem` again.

### Testcase Gist URL

```js
const { app, Tray, Menu, nativeImage } = require('electron');
app.on('ready', () => {
  const t = new Tray(nativeImage.createFromPath('icon.png'));
  t.setContextMenu(Menu.buildFromTemplate([{ label: 'Quit', role: 'quit' }]));
});
```

Per-version result against a watcher that resolves items the way the GNOME extension does:

| version | RegisterStatusNotifierItem argument | result |
|---|---|---|
| 42.10.0 | `:1.1` | ok |
| 43.4.0, 44.0.0-beta.5 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` | registered (menu issue is #52674) |
| 43.4.1, 44.0.0-beta.6, 44.0.0 | `org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1/StatusNotifierItem/1` | `NameHasNoOwner`, registration refused |

nodes.body:

### Electron Version

44.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble), Linux 7.0.0-30-generic, X11 via Xvfb

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

No reliable last-known-working Electron version. The failure is intermittent and has not been compared against a controlled older-Electron matrix.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Under the stated packaged-AppImage startup conditions, Electron should initialize Fontconfig, start the main process, and create the first BrowserWindow without terminating.

### Actual Behavior

The Electron browser/main process intermittently exits with SIGTRAP during application startup.

The failure has been observed in independent command-line startup cases that use valid debug-level options and valid diagnostic-log-directory options. The fully symbolicated instance occurred while a valid debug-level startup case was initializing; other instances occurred after internal service readiness while creating the first BrowserWindow.

This is a native SIGTRAP from Electron/Chromium PartitionAlloc, not a harness timeout, SIGTERM cleanup, OOM event, disk-full event, or GPU-process failure.

### Testcase Gist URL

No public testcase is currently available because the packaged application is closed source.  The failure is reproduced by repeatedly launching one retained Linux AppImage through the sequential startup matrix described in Additional Information. A matching Crashpad minidump, full symbolicated output, and a retained-binary reproduction environment are available privately on maintainer request.

### Additional Information

## Summary

This is an intermittent native `SIGTRAP` from Electron `44.0.0` on Ubuntu `24.04.4`.

Electron's matching public Linux x64 symbols resolve the crash to `partition_alloc::internal::FreelistCorruptionDetected`. Detection occurs when Fontconfig calls `strdup()` while parsing font XML configuration.

This identifies where Electron detected invalid allocator freelist metadata. It does **not** prove that Fontconfig, Pango, or Expat made the earlier invalid write or free.

## Environment

- Electron: `44.0.0`
- Electron public-symbol debug ID: `E798769358C1C954E22B4446B9C113EB0`
- OS: Ubuntu `24.04.4 LTS` (Noble)
- Kernel: `7.0.0-30-generic`
- Architecture: x64
- Display: X11 via Xvfb
- Virtualization: VirtualBox
- VM memory: 5 GiB
- Virtual GPU acceleration: disabled

Relevant Ubuntu packages:

- fontconfig: `2.15.0-1.1ubuntu2`
- libfontconfig1: `2.15.0-1.1ubuntu2`
- libpango-1.0-0: `1.52.1+ds-1build1`
- libpangoft2-1.0-0: `1.52.1+ds-1build1`
- libexpat1: `2.6.1-2ubuntu0.4`

## Controlled Reproduction Process

The product is a closed-source Linux AppImage. I do not yet have a standalone public reproducer.

The failure is captured using one retained AppImage, so no rebuild occurs between attempts:

1. Extract the AppImage once with `--appimage-extract`.
2. Run the extracted `AppRun` repeatedly.
3. Use one Xvfb display and one D-Bus session for a run.
4. Use a minimal Fontconfig configuration containing only system font directories, then run `fc-cache -f`.
5. Start only one application process at a time.
6. Give each launch a fresh temporary data directory, XDG cache/config/runtime directories, diagnostic directory, loopback ports, and process group.
7. Wait up to 120 seconds for the startup-ready record. On successful readiness, request orderly shutdown. Stop the stress run at the first `SIGTRAP`.

The fully symbolicated crash occurred during this valid startup invocation:

    AppRun --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --disable-dev-shm-usage --disable-software-rasterizer -- --backend-debug info --frontend-debug off --profile-log <temporary-profile-path>

This invocation starts the application normally, applies valid command-line debug settings, and waits for the startup-ready record. It does not load user projects, measurement data, remote content, or application workflows.

The packaged Linux AppImage uses `--no-sandbox`. The following flags are CI-specific and have not yet been individually removed from the reproduction:

- `--disable-gpu`
- `--disable-dev-shm-usage`
- `--disable-software-rasterizer`

## Observed Frequency

The retained Electron 44 AppImage completed 99 complete sequential startup stress runs successfully. Attempt 100 then failed during another valid startup case using a diagnostic log-directory argument.

The following reduced observed frequency but did not eliminate the crash:

- increasing VM memory;
- reducing concurrent VM activity;
- serializing application launches;
- reusing one Xvfb/D-Bus session;
- using a minimal Fontconfig configuration;
- prewarming the Fontconfig cache.

An isolated Expat `2.8.3` build was also tested. `ldd` confirmed that Electron and Fontconfig loaded the replacement `libexpat.so.1`, but the same native `SIGTRAP` occurred. This rejects Expat replacement as a fix.

## Fully Symbolicated Crashing Thread

    partition_alloc::internal::FreelistCorruptionDetected
    partition_alloc::PartitionRoot::Alloc
    malloc
    libc.so.6!__GI___strdup
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcExprCreateString
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcParseFamily
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcEndElement
    libexpat.so.1
    libfontconfig.so.1!FcConfigParseAndLoadFromMemoryInternal

The Crashpad dump shows:

- process uptime: approximately 8 seconds;
- `SIGTRAP`, not `SIGSEGV`;
- crash in the Electron browser/main process, not a renderer or GPU subprocess;
- no OOM, disk-full, GPU, or test-harness-timeout event.

## Questions

1. Does this match a known Electron/Chromium Linux PartitionAlloc or allocator-shim issue involving system Fontconfig/Pango libraries?
2. Is packaged AppImage `--no-sandbox` behavior relevant to this allocation path?
3. Which supported Electron or Chromium diagnostics can identify the earlier allocation, free, or write that corrupted the freelist before `malloc()` detected it?
4. Is there a later Electron or Chromium branch with a relevant Linux allocator fix that should be tested?

## Potentially Related Report

This may be related at the environment and symptom level, but has not been proven to be the same root cause:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322185

## Evidence Availability

A matching Crashpad `.dmp`, complete symbolicated output, sanitized command line, and additional environment details are available through a private maintainer-requested channel.

I will not publish the raw minidump, system core, packaged binary, source code, or CI evidence directory publicly.

## Analysis Note

This report was heavily AI-assisted. The underlying evidence was independently captured and verified through retained-AppImage startup loops, Crashpad minidumps, systemd core metadata, official Electron 44 symbols, exact package versions, and the resolved native stack.

Please treat the causal interpretation as a diagnostic lead. Corrections, requests for non-sensitive evidence, and guidance toward a supported minimal reproducer are welcome.

### Problem Description

Hi,

On Wayland, CJK input methods currently only get a cursor rectangle from the app. Because the cursor moves while typing Pinyin, the candidate popup jumps around constantly.

The proposed fix in wayland-protocols is to let apps also send a preedit rectangle, so the input method can anchor the popup to the start of the preedit instead of the moving cursor. See the discussion here:
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/517
https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wayland/wayland-protocols/-/merge_requests/521

Since Electron apps like VS Code and Slack are very popular on Linux, it would make a huge difference if Electron could send the preedit rectangle via zwp_text_input_v3 (in addition to the cursor rectangle). Without that, input methods can't fix the jumping even if they support the new protocol.

Is there any plan to implement this? I'd be glad to test an early build.

Thanks!


This also affects Chromium upstream. I tried to file an issue at [issues.chromium.org](https://issues.chromium.org/) but couldn't log in. If anyone from the Electron team can help pass this along to the Chromium input team, that would be great.



### Proposed Solution

input methods

input methods

nodes.title: Guidance / workaround request: macOS 15+ CJK font rendering corruption (upstream Chromium hvgl)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker without success

### Problem Description

Electron apps rendering Chinese text on macOS 15+ (Sequoia / Tahoe) can hit CJK glyph corruption when the system font subsystem is in certain states. The root cause is upstream: macOS 15 introduced the private `hvgl` outline format used exclusively by PingFangUI.ttc, and `CGFontCreateWithDataProvider()` returns nil for hvgl bytes. Skia's cross-process typeface reconstruction falls back to family-name lookup, which can pick a different PingFang variant than the one used for shaping, producing a stable per-character CID mismatch (e.g. 工 → ┥, 作 → ﬄ, 辛 → 扳, 苦 → 梧, 了 → Y).

This has been observed across Electron 19 (Chromium 102), Electron 22 (Chromium 108), and Electron 38 (Chromium ~130). Chromium has a partial fix in `printing/common/metafile_utils.cc:490` (see [455517173 comment 4](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173) and fix [8007770](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8007770)) but this only covers the printing path; the on-screen rendering path is still affected on current Chromium.


### Proposed Solution

Any of the following would help downstream apps:

1. **Documentation**: Add a note to Electron macOS docs about the recommended CJK-safe `font-family` stack pattern (put `"PingFang SC"` before `-apple-system` to force run-level match and avoid the Blink char-level fallback path that triggers the mismatch). This is the simplest and confirmed effective workaround.

2. **Cherry-pick evaluation**: Consider evaluating whether the Chromium `metafile_utils.cc:490` fix (or similar rendering-path workaround if/when Chromium lands one) should be backported to Electron LTS branches.

3. **Optional runtime flag**: A CLI flag like `--force-native-cjk-render` that routes CJK glyph rasterization through CoreText's high-level APIs (which handle hvgl natively) instead of the byte-stream serialization path.

Option 1 is the lowest-cost and would help many downstream apps immediately.

### Alternatives Considered

- CSS-only fix in each app: put `PingFang SC` first in the `font-family` stack. Appears to help in the cases we've tested, but we haven't verified this rigorously across every affected Electron/macOS combination. Also requires every affected app to figure this out independently.
- Wait for Apple to publish the hvgl spec: HarfBuzz maintainers have been waiting since 2024; no public timeline that we're aware of.
- Embed a fallback font (e.g. Noto Sans SC) with probe-based auto-heal: adds several MB per app and requires runtime detection logic.

### Additional Information

Related upstream references:
- Chromium: [#380313555](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/380313555), [#455517173](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173)
- HarfBuzz: [#4891](https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/4891)
- FreeType: [#1281](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/freetype/freetype/-/issues/1281)
- fonttools: [#3639](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/issues/3639)
- Apple HVF partial docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hvf

Other apps hitting the same underlying macOS font issue via different code paths: mpv, Servo, Godot, Jellyfin Swiftfin, Parley/Blitz.

Even a short "this is out of scope for Electron, please file with Chromium/Apple" response with any suggested best practice would be genuinely helpful for downstream apps stuck in this workaround limbo.

nodes.title: macOS 15+ CJK garbling in Electron via system PingFang font (upstream Chromium hvgl)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker without success

### Electron Version

22.3.27 (also seen on 19.1.9)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.x and Tahoe 26.4.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Not tied to Electron version - triggered by macOS 15+ font subsystem behavior.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

Chinese text like "工作辛苦了" renders correctly in Electron app windows.

### Actual Behavior

On some macOS 15+ machines, CJK characters render as unrelated glyphs. Real-world user screenshots show a stable per-character mapping:

```
工 → ┥
作 → ﬄ
辛 → 扳
苦 → 梧
了 → Y
```

The corruption is intermittent - triggered by macOS font subsystem state (both PingFangUI.ttc and AssetsV2 PingFang.ttc present). Restarting the Electron app usually recovers.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Root cause is upstream in Chromium/Skia, not Electron-specific. Chromium already has partial handling in `printing/common/metafile_utils.cc:490` (see [chromium/455517173 comment4](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173) and fix [8007770](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8007770)). The rendering path in main Chromium is still affected.

Filing here for visibility and to check if Electron would consider a backport/workaround for supported branches. If out of scope for Electron, please redirect.

<details><summary>In-depth investigation</summary>

macOS 15 introduced the private `hvgl` outline table used exclusively by PingFangUI.ttc. `CGFontCreateWithDataProvider()` returns nil on the raw hvgl bytes. When Chromium/Skia falls back to `MakeFromName("PingFang SC")` for cross-process rasterization, it can resolve to AssetsV2's PingFang.ttc (CFF format), whose glyph table layout differs entirely from PingFangUI's. The result: text shape produces glyph IDs from PingFangUI's cmap (e.g., 工 → gid 695), which are then rendered against AssetsV2's glyph table (where gid 695 corresponds to ┥).

Minimal API-level reproducer (any macOS 15+):

```swift
import Foundation
import CoreText
let path = "/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Versions/A/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc"
let data = NSData(contentsOfFile: path)!
let provider = CGDataProvider(data: data as CFData)!
print(CGFont(provider) as Any)  // nil
print(CTFontManagerCreateFontDescriptorsFromData(data as CFData) as Any)  // 0 descriptors
```

Related upstream references:
- Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/380313555, https://issues.chromium.org/issues/455517173
- HarfBuzz: https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/issues/4891
- FreeType: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/freetype/freetype/-/issues/1281
- Fonttools: https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools/issues/3639
- Apple HVF docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/hvf

Other applications hitting the same underlying macOS font issue via different code paths: mpv, Servo, Godot, Jellyfin Swiftfin, Parley/Blitz.

</details>

nodes.title: [Bug]: Tray StatusNotifierItem answers property reads on its well-known name but errors on its unique name, breaking GNOME AppIndicator
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [X] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [X] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [X] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.4.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu, Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Reproduced on two independent stacks: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS / GNOME 46 / Wayland / kernel 6.8, and Linux Mint 22.3 / Cinnamon / X11 / kernel 6.8.0-136. Tray hosts `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` and `xapp-sn-watcher` (xapps 3.2.2) respectively.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

28.3.3

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A `Tray`'s StatusNotifierItem should answer `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get` and `GetAll` regardless of whether the request is addressed to its well-known name (`org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1`) or to that name's unique connection name (`:1.NNN`). Per the D-Bus specification a unique name and any well-known name the connection owns are equivalent destinations.

This matters because GDBus clients routinely resolve a well-known name to its unique owner before querying, to avoid races if ownership changes. Both tray hosts tested do exactly that, so the unique-name path is the only one they ever use.

### Actual Behavior

Property reads succeed on the well-known name and fail on the unique name — same process, same object path, same interface, same moment, only the destination differs:

| Call on `/StatusNotifierItem`, iface `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem` | via well-known name | via unique name `:1.1219` |
|---|---|---|
| `Properties.GetAll` | OK — 14 properties | **FAIL** |
| `Properties.Get(Status)` | OK | **FAIL** |
| `dbusmenu.GetLayout` | OK | OK |

```
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
```

`:1.1219` is confirmed via `GetNameOwner` to be the owner of that well-known name — it is not a different connection. Note the **menu object answers on both addresses; only the `Properties` interface on `/StatusNotifierItem` discriminates.** The menu is still unreachable in practice, because the host learns the menu's path from the `Menu` property it can never read.

**This is a regression, and the behavioural difference is the well-known name itself:**

| | Electron 28.3.3 (works) | Electron 43.4.0 (broken) |
|---|---|---|
| Well-known name | **none — unique only** | `StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1` |
| `GetAll` via unique name | OK — 14 properties | **FAIL** |
| Menu object path | `/com/canonical/dbusmenu` | `/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1` |
| Host outcome | icon + menu | neither |

Electron 28 registered no well-known name at all, so hosts addressed the unique name that already works. Electron 43 registers one and then refuses reads to its own unique owner.

**Control** — a non-Electron indicator on the same session answers the same call shape on its unique name:

```
Get(Id) via :1.115 /org/ayatana/NotificationItem/livepatch -> (<'livepatch'>,)
```

**Host-side confirmation**, `xapp-sn-watcher` with `sn-watcher-debug true`:

```
create_key: Key: 'org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-261894-1/StatusNotifierItem'
sync_skeleton: Syncing icon properties (org.freedesktop.statusnotifieritem-261894-1)
** CRITICAL **: Could not get properties for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-261894-1:
GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in GetAll
… no set_icon_from_pixmap, no update_menu — the item is never populated
```

The same watcher on the Electron 28 build, and on other pixmap-only items such as `flameshot` and `copyq`, completes normally.

On GNOME the equivalent failure is raised in `appIndicator.js:_checkNeededProperties` via `statusNotifierWatcher.js:_registerItem`, and in one run the exception left the extension INACTIVE for the rest of the session — removing the tray for **every other app** too.

User-visible outcome: no icon, or a generic missing-image placeholder, and no context menu.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Why "I don't know how to test" for Chrome.** The menu object path moving to `/org/chromium/DbusMenu/1` in the affected version suggests this lives in Chromium's `StatusIconLinuxDbus` backend rather than in Electron's wrapper, and I would expect it to be a Chromium bug. But Chrome does not expose a tray icon in normal desktop use, so I could not construct an equivalent reproduction to confirm it before filing. If a maintainer can confirm the backend, this should be moved to the Chromium tracker — I am happy to refile there.

**Reproduction** with any Electron app that creates a `Tray`, on a session with an SNI host:

1. Find the item's bus name: `gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.ListNames | tr ',' '\n' | grep StatusNotifierItem`
2. Read a property via that well-known name — succeeds:
   ```
   gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 \
     --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
     --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
   ```
3. Resolve the unique owner: `... --method org.freedesktop.DBus.GetNameOwner <well-known-name>`
4. Repeat step 2 against `:1.NNN` — errors.

Steps 2 and 4 are the whole report; the asymmetry between them is the bug.

**Ruled out**, each tested directly against live 28.3.3 and 43.4.0 instances running concurrently on the same machine and session:

- Missing `IconName` / `IconThemePath` — both builds omit them; hosts fall back to `IconPixmap` cleanly, as they do for other apps.
- Empty D-Bus introspection — both builds return `<node></node>`; the hosts do not introspect.
- The icon asset — byte-identical between the two builds, and it renders correctly from the 28.3.3 item.
- A startup race — polling `GetAll` from the instant the bus name appears returns success at t+0ms on the working build, and the failure on 43.4.0 is permanent and reproducible minutes later.
- Wrong interface name — hosts correctly use `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem`.
- Stale registration, desktop shell state, corrupted user config — excluded by restarting app, tray host and shell.

**Workaround, for anyone finding this:** none from application code. There is no command-line switch to suppress the well-known name registration. Not registering one — as Electron 28 did — would sidestep the defect entirely, since clients would then address the unique name that already answers.

Credit: the Cinnamon/X11 measurements, the 28-vs-43 bus-registration comparison and the watcher logs come from a user of my app investigating the regression on his own machine.

### Operating System Version

Unknown — not bisected. Reported by a user upgrading an app from Electron 28.3.3 to 43.4.0.

### Expected Behavior

A `Tray`'s StatusNotifierItem should answer `org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get` / `GetAll` regardless of whether the request is addressed to its well-known name (`org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1`) or to that name's unique connection name (`:1.NNN`). They are the same connection, so both destinations must resolve to the same object and return the same properties.

This matters because GNOME's `ubuntu-appindicators` / `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` resolves the service to its unique name before reading properties, so the unique-name path is the only one it ever uses.

### Actual Behavior

Property reads succeed on the well-known name and fail on the unique name, for both `Get` and `GetAll`:

```
$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 \
    --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
(<'..._status_icon_1'>,)

$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.558 \
    --object-path /StatusNotifierItem \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get

$ gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1 ... GetAll
(full property dict)

$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.558 ... GetAll
Error: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get
```

`:1.558` is the unique owner of that well-known name, obtained via `GetNameOwner`.

**Control.** A non-Electron indicator on the same session answers the same call shape on its unique name:

```
$ gdbus call --session --dest :1.115 \
    --object-path /org/ayatana/NotificationItem/livepatch \
    --method org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get org.kde.StatusNotifierItem Id
(<'livepatch'>,)
```

**Downstream effect.** `gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` resolves to the unique name (`statusNotifierWatcher.js` → `Util.getUniqueBusName`) and then requires `['Id', 'Menu']` in `appIndicator.js:_checkNeededProperties`. It therefore always takes the failing path and throws:

```
While initalizing proxy for org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-1:
Gio.DBusError: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.Failed: error occurred in Get
  getProperty@.../dbusProxy.js:89:33
  refreshProperty@.../appIndicator.js:306:48
  _checkNeededProperties@.../appIndicator.js:505:66
  _registerItem@.../statusNotifierWatcher.js:95:31
  RegisterStatusNotifierItemAsync@.../statusNotifierWatcher.js:205:24
```

Visible outcomes varied between runs of the same build:

- the item never registers with the watcher and no icon appears at all;
- the item registers but has no readable properties, and the panel draws a generic missing-image placeholder;
- **in one run the exception left the extension INACTIVE for the remainder of the session, removing the tray for every other app too.**

Because `Menu` is one of the properties that cannot be read, `setContextMenu()` is also unreachable — so the item ends up with no icon, no working activation, and no context menu.

Not investigated: whether other SNI hosts are affected. KDE Plasma has a native host and may address items by well-known name, which would make this present as GNOME-only.

Two hypotheses were tested and ruled out: `Get` is not simply unimplemented (it answers on the well-known name), and it is not a startup race (reads succeed 3 ms after the bus name appears).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Reproduced on 3/3 probes.

The application's own icon file is not involved — it loads with `isEmpty === false`, and the same asset renders correctly on macOS and Windows builds of the same app.

To reproduce with any Electron app that creates a `Tray` on a GNOME/Wayland session with the AppIndicator extension enabled:

1. Launch the app and find its SNI bus name: `gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.ListNames | tr ',' '\n' | grep StatusNotifierItem`
2. Read a property via that well-known name — succeeds.
3. Resolve the unique owner: `gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.DBus --object-path /org/freedesktop/DBus --method org.freedesktop.DBus.GetNameOwner <well-known-name>`
4. Read the same property via the unique name — errors.
5. `journalctl --user -b | grep -i statusnotifier` shows the extension's proxy-initialisation failure.

Steps 2 and 4 are the whole report: the asymmetry between them is the bug.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 40.10.2 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.1.8-1-cachyos, KDE Plasma on **Wayland** (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland), NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, 4K display (3840×2160). ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version Not known — not tested in an older version. ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior A `webContents.sendInputEvent({ type: 'mouseDown'/'mouseUp', x, y, button: 'left' })` mouse click at `(x, y)` should be received by the page at `(x, y)`, so the element at that point is clicked. ### Actual Behavior The click is received by the page at a **mis-scaled position**. # [Bug] `webContents.sendInputEvent` mouse coordinates are mis-scaled by `devicePixelRatio` under fractional-DPR on Linux/Wayland

## Environment
- **OS:** CachyOS (Arch-based), kernel 7.1.8-1-cachyos
- **DE/Session:** KDE Plasma on **Wayland** (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland)
- **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
- **Electron:** 40.10.2
- **Display:** 4K (3840×2160), monitor reports scale `1` (kscreen-doctor: `Scale: 1`), but `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.2559…**

## Summary
`webContents.sendInputEvent()` mouse events (`mouseMove`/`mouseDown`/`mouseUp`) are
dispatched to the page at coordinates that are **divided by the window's
`devicePixelRatio`**. A click sent to `(x, y)` arrives in the page at
`(x/DPR, y/DPR)`, so on a fractional-DPR display every synthetic click lands
~20% short of where it was aimed. Links/nav elements miss, so programmatic
clicking does not work.

## Reproduction (minimal, no app)
```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron')
app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({ width: 900, height: 600, show: false })
  await win.loadURL('https://example.com/')
  console.log('DPR', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('window.devicePixelRatio'))
  await win.webContents.executeJavaScript(`
    window.addEventListener('mousedown', e=>window.__m=[e.clientX,e.clientY], true);
    'ok'`)
  win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseMove', x:200, y:150 })
  win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseDown', x:200, y:150, button:'left', clickCount:1 })
  win.webContents.sendInputEvent({ type:'mouseUp',   x:200, y:150, button:'left', clickCount:1 })
  await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,300))
  console.log('received at', await win.webContents.executeJavaScript('window.__m'))
  app.exit(0)
})
```

## Observed (this machine)
`devicePixelRatio` = 1.2559. Clicks sent to known points are received at ~0.795× (≈ 1/1.256):

| Sent | Page received |
|------|--------------|
| (50,50)   | (39,39)     |
| (100,100) | (79,79)     |
| (200,150) | (159,119)   |
| (400,300) | (318,239)   |

The received coordinates track `sent / devicePixelRatio`. On this fractional-DPR
display the offset is large enough that clicking a normal-sized link hits empty
space, so nothing navigates.

## Additional observations
- Events still arrive as `trusted: true` — the input is genuine, just mis-positioned.
- `pointermove` receives a slightly different coordinate than `mousemove`
  (`149,149` vs `148,148` in one probe), consistent with a DIP↔CSS translation
  happening inside the input pipeline.
- Not related to window zoom: reproduced identically at zoom levels 100% / 90% / 125%.
- **The fractional DPR is triggered by the page itself, not the display config.**
  On this system the compositor reports `Scale: 1` and there is NO global/fractional
  scaling configured (kwinrc `Scale=1`, `Xft.dpi=96`, no `GDK_SCALE`/`QT_SCALE_FACTOR`).
  Yet:
  - `about:blank`  → `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.0** (clean)
  - `example.com`  → `window.devicePixelRatio` = **1.2559** (anomalous)
  Same window, same display. The DPR jumps to the fractional value only when a real
  web page is navigated to. This points at a buffer/scale negotiation that happens
  on page load (Wayland fractional-scaling path), not a user display setting.
- Suspected to be specific to this Linux/Wayland + NVIDIA + fractional-scale path,
  where `scaleFactor` (1) and `devicePixelRatio` (1.256) diverge.

## Expected
A `sendInputEvent` click at `(x, y)` should be received by the page at `(x, y)`.

## Notes for maintainers
Likely the coordinate translation in the renderer input path isn't accounting for
the page's `devicePixelRatio` (the window is scaled to DPR 1.256 while coordinates
are passed in CSS pixels). A workaround on the caller's side is to multiply the
coordinates by `webContents.getZoomFactor()`-adjacent DPR before sending, but the
correct fix is in Electron's input dispatch so `sendInputEvent` coordinates match
the page coordinate space.
